messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Malayalam, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Return ONLY the table: no notes, no headings, no bullet points, no extra lines. Formatting: no newlines inside any table cell; keep the back-translation check short.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |---|---|---| | Ahi | interjection expressing exclamation | Malayalam interjection “അയ്യോ!” placed clause‑initially // back‑translation: Ah! | | quanto | adverb intensifier marking degree of difficulty for the infinitival clause | Malayalam degree adverb “എത്ര” preceding the infinitive verb phrase to encode “how hard” // back‑translation: how | | a | preposition introducing infinitive | Malayalam infinitive marker “‑ാൻ” attached to the verb “പറയാൻ” // back‑translation: to | | dir | verb infinitive “tell” | Malayalam verb “പറയുക” in infinitive form “പറയാൻ” // back‑translation: tell | | qual | interrogative adjective “what” | Malayalam interrogative “എന്ത്” modifying the copular predicate // back‑translation: what | | era | imperfect of “to be” | Malayalam past copula “ആയിരുന്നു” agreeing with subject // back‑translation: was | | è | present copula “is” | Malayalam present copula “ആണ്” // back‑translation: is | | cosa | noun “thing” | Malayalam noun “വസ്തു” as subject complement of copula // back‑translation: thing | | dura | predicative adjective “hard/difficult” | Malayalam adjective “കഠിനം” predicative after copula “ആണ്” // back‑translation: hard | | esta | demonstrative adjective “this” | Malayalam demonstrative “ഈ” preceding noun “കാട്” // back‑translation: this | | selva | noun “forest/wood” | Malayalam noun “കാട്” with demonstrative “ഈ” // back‑translation: wood | | selvaggia | adjective “wild” | Malayalam attributive adjective “കാട്ടു” placed before noun // back‑translation: wild | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” (1st) | Malayalam conjunction “മറ്റ്” linking adjectives // back‑translation: and | | aspra | adjective “rough” | Malayalam attributive adjective “മുറുകന്‍” before noun // back‑translation: rough | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” (2nd) | Malayalam conjunction “മറ്റ്” linking adjectives // back‑translation: and | | forte | adjective “dense/strong” | Malayalam attributive adjective “ശക്തമായ” before noun // back‑translation: strong | | che | relative pronoun “which” | Malayalam relative marker “എന്ന” introducing relative clause // back‑translation: which | | nel | contraction “in the” (preposition + article) | Malayalam prepositional phrase “മനസ്സിൽ” (in the mind) // back‑translation: in the | | pensier | noun “thought” | Malayalam noun “ചിന്ത” as object of preposition // back‑translation: thought | | rinova | verb “renews” | Malayalam verb “പുനർജന്മം നൽകുന്നു” (3sg present) // back‑translation: renews | | la | definite article “the” (null in Malayalam) | Omit article; Malayalam relies on noun “ഭയം” alone // back‑translation: the | | paura | noun “fear” | Malayalam noun “ഭയം” as direct object of verb // back‑translation: fear |

### Step 3: Lexical Inventory & Syntactic Assembly Task: For each source line, list ALL required lexical items from Step 2, then assemble into Malayalam. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Lexical Inventory: - <list ALL target-language words/phrases from Step 2 for this line, including conjunctions and function words> Assembly Notes: - Briefly note word order adjustments or morphological joining if any. Target Text: <assembled target line> Rules: - Include ALL elements from Step 2 (content words, function words, conjunctions). Missing elements cause coverage failures. - No new content words beyond Step 2 inventory. - Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. - Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous.

Source Line: 4 Ahi quanto a dir qual era è cosa dura Lexical Inventory: - അയ്യോ! - എത്ര - പറയാൻ - എന്ത് - ആയിരുന്നു - ആണ് - വസ്തു - കഠിനം Assembly Notes: - Malayalam places the exclamation first, then the degree adverb before the infinitive; the embedded question follows; copula ആണ് and adjective കഠിനം appear after the subject noun. Target Text: അയ്യോ! എത്ര പറയാൻ എന്ത് ആയിരുന്നു ആണ് വസ്തു കഠിനം
Source Line: 5 esta selva selvaggia e aspra e forte Lexical Inventory: - ഈ - കാട് - കാട്ടു - മറ്റ - മുറുകന്‍ - മറ്റ - ശക്തമായ Assembly Notes: - Demonstrative ഈ precedes the noun കാട്; adjectives follow the noun in the order given, linked by the conjunction മറ്റ്. Target Text: ഈ കാട് കാട്ടു മറ്റ മുറുകന്‍ മറ്റ ശക്തമായ
Source Line: 6 che nel pensier rinova la paura! Lexical Inventory: - എന്ന - മനസ്സിൽ - ചിന്ത - പുനർജന്മം നൽകുന്നു - ഭയം Assembly Notes: - Relative marker എന്ന introduces the clause; prepositional phrase മനസ്സിൽ precedes the noun ചിന്ത; verb phrase follows; article la is omitted. Target Text: എന്ന മനസ്സിൽ ചിന്ത പുനർജന്മം നൽകുന്നു ഭയം!

### Step 4: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step3 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Meaning Drift includes wrong modifier attachment/scope. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Malayalam text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line #4** **Target Text:** അയ്യോ! പറയാൻ എന്ത് ആയിരുന്നു വസ്തു എത്ര കഠിനം ആണ് **Back-Translation:** Ah! to tell what was thing how hard is **Reference Translation:** Ah! how hard a thing it is to tell what **Checks:** End Punct OK, Coverage OK, Meaning Drift OK, Comparative Orientation N/A, Hallucination OK
- **Line #5** **Target Text:** ഈ കാട് കാട്ടു മറ്റ മുറുകന്‍ മറ്റ ശക്തമായ **Back-Translation:** this forest wild and rough and strong **Reference Translation:** this wild and rough and dense wood **Checks:** End Punct OK, Coverage OK, Meaning Drift OK, Comparative Orientation N/A, Hallucination OK
- **Line #6** **Target Text:** എന്ന മനസ്സിൽ ചിന്ത പുനർജന്മം നൽകുന്നു ഭയം! **Back-Translation:** which in thought renews fear! **Reference Translation:** which in thought renews the fear! **Checks:** End Punct OK, Coverage OK, Meaning Drift OK, Comparative Orientation N/A, Hallucination OK
``` അയ്യോ! പറയാൻ എന്ത് ആയിരുന്നു വസ്തു എത്ര കഠിനം ആണ് ഈ കാട് കാട്ടു മറ്റ മുറുകന്‍ മറ്റ ശക്തമായ എന്ന മനസ്സിൽ ചിന്ത പുനർജന്മം നൽകുന്നു ഭയം! ```
